name: MSP430G2553IPW20R
title: Ultra-low-power 16-bit mixed-signal microcontroller, 1 KB to 16 KB flash, with optional 10-bit ADC
summary: The MSP430G2x53 and MSP430G2x13 are 16-bit RISC microcontrollers that run from 1.8 V to 3.6 V at up to 16 MHz and draw 230 µA at 1 MHz and 2.2 V, 0.5 µA in standby and 0.1 µA with RAM kept. They carry 1 KB to 16 KB of flash, 256 or 512 bytes of RAM, two 16-bit Timer_A3, a USCI for UART/LIN/IrDA/SPI/I2C, an 8-input comparator and up to 24 capacitive-touch I/O; the G2x53 parts add a 10-bit 200-ksps ADC with internal reference. They come in 20-pin TSSOP and PDIP, 28-pin TSSOP and 32-pin QFN, and are programmed through Spy-Bi-Wire, JTAG or a UART bootloader.

tables.title: Interrupt sources, flags and vectors
rows: Power-up; external reset; Watchdog Timer+; flash key violation; PC out-of-range (1)
NMI; oscillator fault; flash memory access violation
I/O Port P2 (up to eight flags)
I/O Port P1 (up to eight flags)
notes: (1) Fetching an instruction from the peripheral register space (0h to 01FFh) or from an unused address range causes a reset.
(2) Several flags share this source.
(3) (non)-maskable: the module's own enable bit can block the event; the general interrupt enable (GIE) cannot.
(4) The flags sit in the module's own registers.
(5) SPI mode: UCB0RXIFG. I2C mode: UCALIFG, UCNACKIFG, ICSTTIFG, UCSTPIFG.
(6) UART or SPI mode: UCB0TXIFG. I2C mode: UCB0RXIFG, UCB0TXIFG.
(7) Word 0FFDEh is the BSL security key (BSLSKEY): 0xAA55 there turns the BSL off entirely; 0h there stops the flash being erased when a wrong BSL password is given.
(8) Vector words 0FFDEh down to 0FFC0h are unused by the device and may hold program code.

operation.text: MSP430G2153, G2253, G2353, G2453 and G2553 carry a 10-bit 200-ksps SAR ADC10 with internal reference, sample-and-hold and autoscan; MSP430G2213, G2313, G2413 and G2513 are the same without the ADC10. Flash and RAM: G21x3 1 KB and 256 B, G22x3 2 KB and 256 B, G23x3 4 KB and 256 B, G24x3 8 KB and 512 B, G25x3 16 KB and 512 B. MSP430G2113 is also orderable in the 20-pin PDIP. All have two Timer_A3 timers, one USCI_A0 and one USCI_B0, an 8-channel Comparator_A+, a brownout detector and Spy-Bi-Wire emulation. MSP430G2453 and MSP430G2553 also exist as automotive -Q1 versions.

16-bit RISC core with sixteen 16-bit registers: R0 is the PC, R1 the SP, R2 the SR (also constant generator CG1), R3 constant generator CG2, and R4 to R15 are free for general use. A register-to-register operation takes one CPU clock. The instruction set has 51 instructions in three formats with seven address modes for the source and four for the destination; every instruction works on bytes or words. The instruction cycle time is 62.5 ns.

Besides active mode there are five low-power modes, chosen in software. Any interrupt wakes the part, runs its handler and can return it to the low-power mode. AM: every clock runs. LPM0: CPU and MCLK off, ACLK and SMCLK on. LPM1: as LPM0, and the DCO dc generator is also off when the DCO is not used in active mode. LPM2: CPU, MCLK and SMCLK off, DCO dc generator kept on, ACLK on. LPM3: CPU, MCLK, SMCLK and the DCO dc generator off, ACLK on. LPM4: every clock off, the DCO dc generator off and the crystal oscillator stopped.

Vectors and the power-up start address sit from 0FFFFh down to 0FFC0h; each holds the 16-bit address of its handler. When the reset vector at 0FFFEh reads 0FFFFh (an unprogrammed part) the CPU enters LPM4 straight after power-up. Executing from the peripheral register space (0h to 01FFh) or from an unused address range forces a reset.

A bootloader programs flash or RAM over a UART on P1.1 (transmit) and P1.5 (receive), behind a user password. The word at 0FFDEh (BSLSKEY) controls it: 0xAA55 disables the BSL; 0h prevents a wrong password from erasing the flash. The full protocol is in TI document SLAU319.

Flash is programmed through Spy-Bi-Wire/JTAG or by the CPU in the application, a byte or a word at a time. Main memory is in 512-byte segments; information memory is four 64-byte segments, A to D. Main segments can be erased one at a time or all together; segments A to D may be erased singly or along with main memory. Segment A carries the factory calibration and is locked against program and erase after reset; it can be unlocked, but erasing it loses the calibration. Program and erase need VCC of 2.2 V or more.

The basic clock module has three sources: a 32768-Hz watch-crystal oscillator (LFXT1), the internal low-frequency VLO (about 12 kHz, drawing very little current) and the digitally controlled oscillator (DCO), which starts in under 1 µs. It produces ACLK (from the crystal or the VLO), MCLK for the CPU, and SMCLK for the peripherals. An external digital clock can replace the crystal.

The DCO has 16 ranges set by RSELx, each overlapping the next, and eight taps per range set by DCOx; each tap is a step of SDCO, each range a step of SRSEL. MODx mixes the selected tap with the next one up over 32-clock periods to reach in-between frequencies. RSELx = 14 needs VCC of at least 2.2 V and RSELx = 15 at least 3 V. Factory BCSCTL1/DCOCTL values for 1, 8, 12 and 16 MHz, taken at 3 V and 30°C, are stored in segment A (CALBC1_xMHZ, CALDCO_xMHZ).

Segment A holds the DCO and ADC10 calibration as tag-length-value records: TAG_DCO_30 at 0x10F6 and TAG_ADC10_1 at 0x10DA, with 0xFE marking empty space. The ADC10 record carries offset and gain factors measured with an external 1.5 V reference at 5 MHz, reference factors for 1.5 V and 2.5 V, and temperature-sensor readings at 30°C and 85°C for each reference.

The brownout circuit holds the device in reset while VCC rises and when it falls. The release level, V(B_IT–) plus Vhys(B_IT–), is 1.8 V or less; the CPU starts td(BOR) (2000 µs typical) after VCC passes it. The DCO must keep its default setting until VCC reaches the minimum for the intended clock frequency (6 MHz at 1.8 V, 12 MHz at 2.7 V, 16 MHz at 3.3 V). A short drop of VCC to the VCC(drop) level also causes a reset; that level depends on the width and shape of the drop. A low pulse of at least 2 µs on RST/NMI is accepted as a reset.

Up to three 8-bit ports: P1 and P2 on every package, P3 only on the 28-pin and 32-pin packages. Each bit is set as input or output on its own, has its own selectable pullup or pulldown, and has a pin-oscillator enable for capacitive touch sensing. Every bit of P1 and P2 can raise an interrupt on a chosen edge. On the 20-pin packages, which have no P3 pins, the P3 pulldowns should be turned on (P3REN.x = 1). All outputs together should stay within ±48 mA to hold the VOH and VOL limits.

Setting PxSEL2 with PxSEL cleared turns a pin into an oscillator whose frequency falls as the load capacitance on it rises; the oscillation is routed to Timer_A (TACLK/INCLK on Timer0, CCI2B) to be counted. Up to 24 pins can do this.
The watchdog resets the system when its interval runs out without being serviced. It can be stopped, or used instead as an interval timer that raises an interrupt.

Timer0_A3 and Timer1_A3 are 16-bit counters with three capture/compare registers each, for capture, PWM and interval timing. Interrupts come from counter overflow and from each capture/compare register.

USCI_A0 does UART, enhanced UART with automatic baud-rate detection (LIN), IrDA encode/decode and 3- or 4-wire SPI. USCI_B0 does 3- or 4-wire SPI and I2C. The UART bit clock reaches 2 MBaud; above 1 MBaud the DCO wake-up time counts when the part sleeps in LPM3 or LPM4. I2C runs up to 400 kHz.

An analog comparator for slope-type A/D conversion, battery supervision and watching external signals. Its inputs reach CA0 to CA7; internal references are 0.25 VCC, 0.5 VCC and a diode-based voltage (V(RefVT)); an optional output filter slows the response from 120 ns to 1.5 µs. Its offset can be removed by taking two readings with the inputs exchanged (CAEX) and adding them.

A 10-bit SAR converter with sample select control, an internal 1.5 V or 2.5 V reference and a data transfer controller that stores results to memory without the CPU. Channels A0 to A7 are on P1; channel 10 is the temperature sensor and channel 11 is a VCC/2 divider. The analog supply must be 2.2 V or more; the 2.5 V reference needs 2.9 V or more. The temperature sensor's source impedance is about 51 kΩ and needs a 30 µs sample time. External references go on P1.3 (VEREF–) and P1.4 (VEREF+); in buffered mode (SREF1 = 1, SREF0 = 1) the internal buffer draws IREFB, which REFBURST = 1 limits to the sample and conversion period.

Keep the crystal next to XIN and XOUT with short traces, surround the oscillator pins with ground, keep other clock and data lines and any traces away from under and beside XIN and XOUT, avoid assembly residue or coatings that leak or add capacitance between the pins, and do not take XOUT to the JTAG header. The internal load (XCAPx) is 1, 5.5, 8.5 or 11 pF effective, including about 2 pF of package parasitic per pin; check the actual load by measuring ACLK, and match it to the crystal's specified load.

The device is programmed and debugged by 4-wire JTAG on P1.4 to P1.7 (selected by TEST) or by 2-wire Spy-Bi-Wire on TEST/SBWTCK and RST/NMI/SBWTDIO; no external programming voltage is needed. TEST has an internal pulldown of 25 kΩ to 90 kΩ. After raising TEST, a tool waits at least 1 µs before the first SBWTCK edge. A security fuse, blown by 6 V to 7 V on TEST, permanently cuts off JTAG, Spy-Bi-Wire and emulation access.
The RHB32 exposed pad should be connected to VSS and soldered to the board for heat transfer and mechanical strength.
RAM keeps its contents down to VCC = 1.6 V with the CPU halted; no code may run at that supply.
